what_happened: A batch of disk-fix jobs was drained. One job (20261101-123956-y5q1) actually landed. The drain still counted a red result on the optional pull request head check as a failure, so the batch was recorded as "failed twice". The optional check was red because it refuses records of jobs held for low disk. The the person running Athena logged this as an intervention, saying it was not their mistake, and queued a fix for both problems.
cause: Athena does not separate required checks from optional ones, and it does not check a job's landed state against its recorded outcome. The drain takes any red check as failure. The optional head check also does not know about the records written for jobs held for low disk, so it flags a normal state as invalid. Two parts of the pipeline disagree about what counts as a failure, and nothing reconciles them. Only the the person running Athena's reading of the result catches it.
prevention: Two code changes. First, the drain decides a job's outcome from the job's own state (landed or not) and from required checks only. A red optional check is shown as a warning and never turns a landed job into a failure. Second, the optional pull request head check accepts the records of jobs held for low disk. Add a test that drains a landed job whose optional check is red and expects the outcome "landed", plus a test that the head check passes on a low-disk hold record.
proposed_request: Fix two linked faults. (1) The queue drain must record a job's outcome from the job's own state and its required checks only. A job that landed must never be recorded as failed, and the batch must not stop, because an optional pull request check is red. Show the red optional check as a warning in the drain output. (2) The optional pull request head check must accept the records of jobs held for low disk instead of refusing them. Acceptance: a test drains a landed job whose optional check is red and expects the outcome landed and the batch continuing; a test runs the head check on a branch holding a low-disk hold record and expects a pass; the existing required-check behavior is unchanged, so a red required check still counts as a failure.
